# Official Red Square backend endpoint

Observed **2026-10-08, 23:19–23:21 UTC**, using public first-party HTTP assets
and ordinary TLS handshakes only. No Saito application execution, saved browser
options, local node configuration, wallet, database or environment was inspected.
No WebSocket upgrade, Saito peer authentication, Archive RPC or transaction
broadcast was performed. No service or configuration changes.

## Endpoint established by the public browser contract

**Use `wss://saito.io/wsopen`.** The equivalent explicit-port form generated by
the browser is `wss://saito.io:443/wsopen`.

The unauthenticated public [browser configuration](https://saito.io/options)
returned HTTP 200 directly at the same URL. Its `peers` array advertised one
peer, with these public fields only:

```json
{"host":"saito.io","port":443,"protocol":"https","synctype":"lite"}
```

This was a public GET used by the browser, not a read of a saved options file.
Only the peer fields were extracted; the response was not copied into this
repository. The public [Red Square page](https://saito.io/redsquare/) returned
200 directly and referenced `/saito/saito.js?build=1791446074`. Its
[served bundle](https://saito.io/saito/saito.js?build=1791446074) and
[public source map](https://saito.io/saito/saito.js.map) establish the link:

- Embedded `dist/bundler/default/lib/saito/storage.ts:54` fetches `/options`.
- That source at lines 60–63, and
  `dist/bundler/default/apps/browser/index.ts:24–29`, derive
  `wss://<host>:<port>/wsopen` when the peer protocol is `https`.
- Storage lines 80–104 may retain nonempty cached browser peer settings. This
  finding identifies the currently advertised fresh-browser peer, not every
  existing user's cached selection. No cached state was read.

The bundle was 9,632,005 bytes, SHA-256
`754087df8c15863a6c2f82f84848de05af75ea1b3e4982ba96bca96a52733788`.
The map was 31,156,109 bytes, SHA-256
`517cdb94d9ee91310e55c499882091fe393d7bcbab0403fea376cf2bf1857ba0`.
These observations match the earlier bundle evidence in
[version provenance](SAITO_VERSION_PROVENANCE.md), but do not identify an exact
deployed Git revision. The pinned
[server upgrade route](https://github.com/SaitoTech/saito/blob/9a4ca7e9442eb5e872168ced361ce741d7d139d7/node/lib/saito/core/server.ts#L73)
also uses `/wsopen`; the currently served configuration and URL derivation,
rather than the historical pin alone, establish the official endpoint above.

The owner's [public browser configuration](https://saito.davidengelen.nl/options)
likewise returned 200 directly and advertised
`host=saito.davidengelen.nl`, `port=443`, `protocol=https`, `synctype=lite`.
This agrees with the known public contract
**`wss://saito.davidengelen.nl/wsopen`**. Its
[Red Square page](https://saito.davidengelen.nl/redsquare/) returned 200 directly
and referenced build `1790715873`. This contrast concerns public endpoint
selection only, not equivalent feed history, moderation or service health.

## Redirects and TLS observations

Ordinary HTTP **HEAD** requests produced these results, with automatic
redirect following disabled:

| URL | Status | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `http://saito.io/redsquare/` | 302 | `https://saito.io/redsquare/` |
| `https://saito.io/redsquare` | 301 | `/redsquare/` |
| `http://saito.io/wsopen` | 302 | `https://saito.io/wsopen` |
| `https://saito.io/wsopen` | 404 | None |
| `http://saito.davidengelen.nl/wsopen` | 200 | None |
| `https://saito.davidengelen.nl/wsopen` | 200 | None |

These are observations of the public hosts and paths above, not WebSocket
handshake results. A bare HEAD lacks WebSocket Upgrade headers; the official
404 does not contradict its advertised WSS contract. Likewise the owner's
200 is not evidence of a successful WebSocket upgrade. Use direct WSS on port
443; an HTTP redirect is not a substitute for a verified WSS connection.

Python's default trusted TLS context, with hostname verification enabled and
SNI set to each hostname, accepted both certificates on port 443. Both
connections negotiated TLS 1.3 and `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`:

| Host | Verified certificate SAN | Issuer | Certificate validity UTC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `saito.io` | `saito.io` | Let's Encrypt YR2 | 2026-08-16 14:59:22 through 2026-11-14 14:59:21 |
| `saito.davidengelen.nl` | `saito.davidengelen.nl` | Let's Encrypt YE1 | 2026-08-25 21:03:22 through 2026-11-23 21:03:21 |

Certificates can rotate; these results describe this VPS's trusted TLS path
at the observed time, not every Android device's future trust state. No
certificate pin or backend identity key is inferred from them.

## Verification boundary

This establishes the official **publicly configured endpoint** and successful
ordinary HTTPS/TLS access. It establishes neither a live native WSS upgrade
nor Saito peer identity authentication, Archive availability, returned feed
rows, signature validity, request correlation or transaction acceptance.
Those require the authenticated read verification described in the
[native feed contract](NATIVE_FEED_CONTRACT.md) and
[protocol reference](NATIVE_SAITO_PROTOCOL.md#websocket-handshake-and-archive-requests).
HTTP readiness must not be recorded as successful native feed integration.
